reconciled.notes: Every A and B key is accounted for in an objective's "from"; nothing is rejected and every exercise item and worked example sits in exactly one objective. A3 (height of a building from the angle of elevation, using tangent) is folded into the sides objective, because B1 explicitly covers heights of a kite, building or wall and puts WE3, Ex11-1:2 and Ex11-1:5 there; A3's definition evidence for the angle of elevation is reused as evidence for the elevation/depression objective. The statement for the angles objective is A2's wording rather than B2's, since B2's Pythagoras clause does not fit "from two known sides". The elevation/depression objective has no Ex11-1 items: both finders agree that none of Ex11-1:1-6 tests it, and its exercise evidence comes from end-of-chapter items only.

checks.note: a0009 opens 'As revision' and recalls the three trig ratios; solving for a side in the kite example (a0026) uses sin/cos as ratios of opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse.
The same 'As revision' recall of the ratios (a0009). WE2 (a0027) writes sin ABE = opposite/hypotenuse = 3/4 to find an angle, so it uses the ratio definition.
The revision of the ratios (a0009) is recalled. WE4 (a0029) applies tan DBE = DE/BD, the ratio definition, inside the elevation/depression problem.
WE1 (a0026) and WE5 (a0030) both start with the step of identifying the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse sides. That is the labelling skill, used as a step. Both quotes are present.
WE3 (a0028) has the explicit step 'Identify the opposite and adjacent sides and the hypotenuse' before applying tan, in an angle-of-elevation problem. The quote is present.
WE1 (a0026) chooses the appropriate ratio and solves for h and d, which is the side-calculation method. Ex11-1:1 (a0031) asks for a height, which needs that method. Both quotes are present.

WE3 (a0028) has a known side and an angle, and sets up tan with 'rearrange and solve for h'. WE4 (a0029) computes the sides with tan after saying 'we can calculate the sides', so it uses the side-calculation method as a step.

WE2 (a0027) picks sin from the given sides, then inverts it to get the angle (48,59...), which is the inverse-ratio method for angles. Ex11-1:3 (a0033) asks for the angle of elevation from two sides. Both quotes are present.
a0011 says the ratios and 'the theorem of Pythagoras' will be used to solve problems. WE2 (a0027) uses Pythagoras to find BE as a step in an angle problem. Both quotes are present.

a0021 and a0022 state that two lines are parallel, and 'Notice that alpha=theta' follows from that parallelism. This is the alternate-angles fact applied as a step, although the text does not name it. Both quotes are present. This is the least explicit link of the ten.
